s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic papular eruption with annular lesions and characteristic histopathological features
salient_findings: Rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules on extremities
Erythematous, annular papules with scattered brown flat papules on the face
Histopathology showing hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, and cornoid lamellae
key_facts: Female patient in her 50s
3-month history of symptoms
No remarkable medical or family history
No concurrent medications
Previous treatment with topical steroid ointments and oral compound glycyrrhizin tablets had no effect
Lesions measure up to 5 mm wide
Palms, soles, and oral mucosa not involved
Laboratory tests showed no abnormal findings
Histopathology revealed mild hyperkeratosis, atrophy of the epidermis, and individual cell dyskeratosis

shortlist.label: Disseminated superficial actinic porokeratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Characteristic histopathological features and clinical presentation of pruritic papular eruption with annular lesions

shortlist.label: Eruptive pruritic papular porokeratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and histopathological features match the case, including hyperkeratosis and individual cell dyskeratosis

shortlist.label: Linear porokeratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological features of cornoid lamellae and hyperkeratosis are consistent with porokeratosis, although clinical presentation is less typical

shortlist.label: Porokeratosis of Mibelli
shortlist.why_kept: Characteristic histopathological features, but less common and typically presents with larger lesions

shortlist.label: Flegel's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of pruritic papules and histopathological features of hyperkeratosis and individual cell dyskeratosis are consistent with this rare disease

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules, lack of response to previous treatments, and specific histopathological findings such as cornoid lamellae and individual cell dyskeratosis are consistent with Eruptive pruritic papular porokeratosis (EPPP).

rejected.label: Disseminated superficial actinic porokeratosis
rejected.why: While it shares some histopathological features, DSAP typically has a stronger association with sun-exposed areas and lacks the intense pruritus described in this case.

rejected.label: Linear porokeratosis
rejected.why: Linear porokeratosis presents with lesions that follow the lines of Blaschko, which is not mentioned in the case description.

rejected.label: Porokeratosis of Mibelli
rejected.why: Porokeratosis of Mibelli typically presents with larger, more localized lesions and often starts in childhood, which does not match the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Flegel's disease
rejected.why: Flegel's disease is characterized by a distinct pattern of hyperpigmentation and is not typically associated with the histopathological features or pruritic symptoms described in this case.
